summary: John Drake worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Regent's Park College and the University of Oxford (M.A.). He served at Serampore College (1910–1926) and at Saharanpur Theological Seminary until 1933.
John Drew Bate was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Regent's Park College from circa 1858 to 1865. He served as a member of the Baptist Missionary Society from 1865 to 1897.

John E. Cort is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned a BA at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and an AM at Harvard University. He was appointed professor at Denison University around 1993.

John F. Richards worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of New Hampshire and UC Berkeley. Richards held academic posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1968–1977) and Duke University (circa 1977–2007).

John Faithfull Fleet worked in Indology and history/archaeology. Educated at UCL and under Theodor Goldstücker, he served in the Indian Civil Service (1865–1897), as Government of India Epigraphist (1883–1886), and as Honorary Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society (1906–1917).
John Firminger Duthie served as Superintendent of the Saharanpur Botanical Garden from circa 1876 to 1903 and as Director of the Botanical Survey of India from circa 1891 to 1902.

John Forbes Royle studied at Addiscombe Military Seminary and the University of Edinburgh. He served as Superintendent of the Saharanpur Botanical Garden (1823–1831), Professor at King's College London (1837–1856), and museum curator at the India Office (circa 1837–1858).
John Forbes White Youngson was an Indologist and linguist who earned his M.A. and D.D. at the University of Aberdeen. He served as a missionary with the Church of Scotland from 1875 to 1907.
John Frederick Browne worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Exeter College, Oxford, and the East India Company College before joining the Bengal Civil Service in 1858.
John Frederick Dickson was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He was educated at Westminster School and completed his B.A. at Christ Church, Oxford, studying there from 1855 to 1859.

John Garrett worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as the first Director of the Central College of Bangalore in 1858 and as Director of Public Instruction for the Department of Public Instruction, Mysore, in 1871.

John George Woodroffe studied at University College, Oxford, and under Sivachandra Vidyarnava. He held posts as a Calcutta High Court judge (circa 1904–1922) and Reader in Indian Law at Oxford (1923–1930).

Hangin studied at Hokkaido, Columbia, and Indiana University. He held posts at Johns Hopkins, Georgetown, UC Berkeley, Columbia, and Indiana University Bloomington (1965–1989), working in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies.
John Graham Drummond was an Indologist and linguist who earned his B.A. and Ph.D. at Christ's College, Cambridge. He served there as Lecturer in Bengali in 1936.

John Greenfield Leonard worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Stanford University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, later holding posts at Wisconsin (1967) and the University of California, San Diego (1968–1973).

John Griffiths was an Indologist and art historian who studied at the Royal College of Art. He held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum, Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy School of Art, and National College of Arts (circa 1880–1895).
John H. Berthrong works in Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies. He completed graduate studies under Alfonso Verdu and was attested as holding a post at Boston University in 1996.
John Hay, who worked in Sinology, completed his M.A. at the University of Aberdeen by 1833. He served as a Fellow at the University of Madras from 1888 to 1889.

Hutton studied at Worcester College, Oxford (D.Sc. 1921). He served in the Indian Civil Service (circa 1909–1936) and was William Wyse Professor of Social Anthropology at the University of Cambridge from 1936 to 1950.

John Henry Piet, an Indologist and philosopher of religion, studied at Hope College, Western Theological Seminary, Hartford Seminary, and Columbia University. He was Professor of English Bible and Mission at Western Theological Seminary from 1960 to 1984.
